issues.description: Holds the literal string 'basic Python' - free text copied from brief.learner_state.known rather than a prerequisite ID. The corresponding entity pre-001 exists and is not referenced here.
Holds 'obj-001', an objective ID in a prerequisite reference field. Same pattern in modules[mod-003].prerequisite_refs and in lessons[les-003-a, les-003-b].

Empty. mod-001 consumes 15 of the 60 minutes and holds four lessons but maps to no supplied objective; its stated purpose is to deliver pre-001..pre-004. The sequencing_rationale asserts 'no orphan modules are introduced', which contradicts the artifact's own shape.
All four carry empty objective_ids. They are reachable through mod-001.lesson_ids, so they are not unreachable, but no lesson in module 1 traces to an objective.

'Rationale is authored by the learner, not copied verbatim from documentation or generated by a tool without attribution' introduces an academic-integrity criterion that appears in no objective and in no success criterion. The packet's own note concedes operationalisation is left to the researcher.

Marked candidate / model_proposed even though brief.learner_state.known explicitly lists 'basic Python'. Conservative rather than overclaiming, so not a provenance violation, but it understates supplied evidence and is what justifies the 15-minute remediation module.
Both assessments are summative; no formative assessment exists anywhere in the artifact and no lesson populates formative_assessment_ids.

technical_review.notes: Objective coverage into modules, lessons and assessments is complete for obj-001 and obj-002, and lesson/module back-references resolve. The defects cluster in the prerequisite reference field, which holds a raw capability string in one place and objective IDs in four others, and in mod-001, which is a fully populated module with no objective mapping. Rubric dimension IDs (rd-001-1..3, rd-002-1..3) are defined and the mastery rules reference them correctly. No validator output was included in the packet, so `validator_appears_correct` is null on every issue; the findings below are the reviewer's own reference walk over the artifact, not a confirmation or contradiction of a quality gate.

special_question.notes: Answered independently of the orphan module and the 'basic Python' reference string. The objectives are the best-written in the set - each one embeds condition, performance and standard in a single sentence, and the success criteria are unambiguously checkable ('code executes without errors', 'at least two transformation strategies'). The rubrics use explicit numeric levels and flag every threshold as provisional. Two reservations are substantial enough to block approval as written. First, instruction and assessment have collapsed into each other: les-002-c has learners practise on the assessment fixture itself, and les-003-b is the act of writing the asmt-002 submission, so there is no independent evidence of learning - the graded artifact is produced under instructional scaffolding. Second, a quarter of the session (mod-001, 15 minutes, four lessons) teaches Python basics, library imports, tabular concepts and file I/O to a learner the brief already describes as knowing basic Python.

rubric_scores.rationale: Both objectives state condition, observable performance and standard in one sentence, and the criteria are binary-checkable: 'at least two transformation strategies are applied', 'the resulting dataset contains no missing or invalid values in the targeted columns', 'code executes without errors'. obj-002 requires rationale 'present for at least every distinct strategy applied', which gives a rater a countable test. No reader would disagree about what counts as success.

asmt-001 to obj-001 and asmt-002 to obj-002, one to one, with evidence statements that restate the success criteria almost verbatim (ev-001-a/b/c against obj-001's three criteria) and rubric dimensions in the same order. Nothing is assessed that is not claimed, apart from ev-002-c.

Code plus cleaned dataset plus written rationale is the right evidence base, and the numeric rubric levels make scoring reproducible. Two deductions: the evidence is produced during instruction rather than independently of it, which weakens any claim the artifact demonstrates unaided capability; and ev-002-c (authorship/attribution) cannot be judged from the artifact at all.

apply for the transformation objective and evaluate for the justification objective is the correct pairing, and the lesson patterns escalate properly within mod-002 (explanation -> worked_example -> guided_practice). obj-002 is tagged knowledge_dimension=conceptual where the reasoning about downstream impact reads closer to metacognitive, and les-003-b's 'reflection' pattern is doing production work rather than reflection.

Five candidates, each with a rationale naming the objective or assessment that generated it, a coherent dependency chain, and teaching_objective_id populated - the only packet that uses that field. Relevance is high and qualification is correct. Loses a point for minimality: pre-005 (basic written English) is a language condition already implied by constraints.language and is not a useful gate, and pre-001 restates evidence the brief already supplies.

Foundations -> apply -> justify is the right dependency order, and the sequencing_rationale correctly explains that justification must follow the choices being justified. The weakness is proportion rather than order: 15 minutes of prerequisite remediation, 30 minutes on obj-001 and 15 minutes on obj-002 leaves the evaluate-level objective the least supported.

Preparation for asmt-001 is thorough - a worked example applying two strategies, then guided practice doing the same. But the alignment is too tight to be valid: les-002-c has learners work the assessment fixture with scaffolding prompts, and les-003-b's activity is literally 'adds inline comments ... to their asmt-001 submission'. Learners are coached through the graded artifact rather than prepared for it, and there is no formative check anywhere to catch problems earlier.

Moderate and concentrated on obj-002. Justification gets one 7-minute explanation and then straight to production, with no worked example of a good rationale and no practice attempt before the graded one. The absence of any formative instrument means the first feedback a learner receives is on the summative.

mod-001 spends a quarter of the session and four separate lessons on Python variables and loops, library imports, tabular concepts and CSV read/write for a learner the brief already places at basic Python. pre-005 adds an English-language gate that no instruction can act on.

Separate the practice fixture from the assessment fixture, cut or compress mod-001 and return the time to obj-002, add a formative check before each summative, remove ev-002-c, and repoint the two prerequisite reference fields. Objectives and rubrics can stand almost unchanged.

prerequisite_acceptance.notes: pre-002 (install/import libraries and read documentation), pre-003 (tabular data concepts) and pre-004 (read and write CSV in Python) are relevant, correctly marked candidate, and each names the objective or assessment that requires it - accepted as written. pre-005 is rejected: 'basic written communication in English sufficient to produce inline comments' is not a verifiable entry condition, duplicates constraints.language, and cannot be remediated or screened in any practical way. pre-001 is accepted in substance but should be reclassified as confirmed, since brief.learner_state.known already lists 'basic Python'; leaving it candidate is what justifies the 15-minute remediation module that inflates the session. All five carry teaching_objective_id, which is good practice but sits oddly with candidate status - an entity cannot simultaneously be an unverified entry gate and a planned teaching target without a stated policy for what happens at intake.

edit_effort.notes: Estimated: ev-002-c removed and one formative added to each assessment path; pre-001 status corrected and pre-005 dropped; mod-001 cut or compressed and mod-003 extended; four module-1 lessons removed or merged and les-002-c repointed to a practice fixture distinct from the assessment fixture. Objectives require no change.

pedagogical_review.overall_notes: The objective and rubric writing here is the strongest in the set - if the packet were judged on those two artifacts alone it would score at the top. What holds it back is structural: a quarter of the session teaches what the learner is said to know, and the final two lessons are the assessment rather than preparation for it, so the design cannot produce independent evidence of learning.
